subject: general
question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **effective rate of interest** for simple interest is calculated as **Rate × Time**.

Effective Rate = 3% × 3 = 9%

**Simple Interest** = 9% of ₹3000

Simple Interest = 0.09 × 3000 = 270

**∴ The correct answer is ₹270.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹3000

**Rate (R)** = 3% per annum

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bcae4ecf8bd8fcd0fa9aa53a4c00be54ca78b236fc8b7af0e306b7a208164e56.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (3000 × 3 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 3000 × 9 ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 30 × 9

⇒ SI = 270

**∴ The correct answer is ₹270.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) to be paid back after the time period is A = Principal + Simple Interest = P × (1 + RT/100).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest is always calculated on the initial **Principal**, whereas in Compound Interest, interest is calculated on the **accumulated amount** of previous years.

Finding Rate or Time

The rate can be found using R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) and time can be found using T = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R).
